**Path prefix: `/.well-known/`**
> "To address these uses, this memo reserves a path prefix in HTTP, HTTPS, WebSocket (WS), and Secure WebSocket (WSS) URIs for these "well-known locations", "/.well-known/"." (Section 1)

It sits at the top of the path only: "/.well-known/example" is a well-known URI, "/foo/.well-known/example" is not (Section 3).

**Registration policy: Specification Required, on the advice of one or more experts**
> "Well-known URIs are registered on the advice of one or more experts, with a Specification Required (using terminology from [RFC8126])." (Section 5.1)

And the obligation on anyone minting one:
> "Applications that wish to mint new well-known URIs MUST register them, following the procedures in Section 5.1, subject to the following requirements." (Section 3)

Registrations go in the IANA "Well-Known URIs" registry, carry a status of "permanent" or "provisional", and must reference a specification. Names must conform to the `segment-nz` production, so no "/" in them.

**URI schemes: http and https by this memo; ws and wss via RFC 8307; others only if their own definitions allow it**
> "This specification updates the "http" [RFC7230] and "https" [RFC7230] schemes to support well-known URIs." (Section 3)

> "Other existing schemes can use the appropriate process for updating their definitions; for example, [RFC8307] does so for the "ws" and "wss" schemes." (Section 3)

> "Well-known URIs can also be used with other URI schemes, but only when those schemes' definitions explicitly allow it." (Section 1)

Table 1 in Section 5.2 lists the schemes already marked as supporting well-known URIs: coap, coap+tcp, coap+ws, coaps, coaps+tcp, coaps+ws, http, https, ws, wss.","structuredOutput":null,"model":"deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017","provider":"neus","zeus":{"reasoning":"The user asks a factual question about RFC 8615.
